summary: Docked Windows machines: Ethernet + Wi‑Fi active -> DNS suffix order causes VPN internal hostname resolution to fail
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple employees on Windows 11 laptops connected to company Thunderbolt docks (Dell WD19TB / WD22) report intermittent inability to resolve internal hostnames (e.g., api.internal.redwood, idp.corp) immediately after docking or waking from sleep. The machines maintain a working VPN session (WireGuard corporate tunnel) but internal hostnames resolve to public IPs or fail with NXDOMAIN, causing service authentication errors (SSO/OIDC token fetch failures) and slowing sign‑on flows.

Impact:
- Affects ~8–12 users in SF office using corporate docks with both Ethernet and Wi‑Fi enabled on the client (AX210/AX201 adapters).
- Users see repeated SSO/popups and tooling that talks to internal services times out (CLI flows, local dev proxies).
- No obvious 5xx server-side errors; services are reachable once DNS resolution is corrected.

Environment:
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise, builds 22621.x and 22631.x
- Docks: Dell WD19TB and WD22, firmware updated Feb 2026
- NICs: Intel AX210 Wi‑Fi adapter + dock Ethernet (Realtek/Intel depending on dock model)
- VPN: WireGuard corporate profile, configured as force-tunnel for all traffic
- Network: office VLANs (prod-us-west-sf-office), internal DNS servers at 10.10.0.10/10.10.0.11

Steps to reproduce (observed reliably on repro devices):
1) Connect a Windows laptop to the Thunderbolt dock with active Wi‑Fi on the laptop.
2) Ensure WireGuard tunnel is up (corporate profile applied).
3) Observe ipconfig /all shows both Ethernet and Wi‑Fi adapters with DNS servers; Windows shows corporate internal DNS on the Ethernet adapter and public DNS on Wi‑Fi (ISP fallback).
4) Try to resolve an internal hostname (nslookup api.internal.redwood). Result: Name resolves to external/public address or NXDOMAIN.
5) Run route print and observe default route coming from WireGuard, but interface metric chooses Ethernet for DNS queries (based on adapter metrics/search suffix ordering).
6) Unplug dock Ethernet or disable Wi‑Fi -> hostname resolution immediately corrects to internal address.

Observed logs / snippets:
- ipconfig /all excerpt (sanitized):
  Ethernet adapter Ethernet (Dock):
    DNS Servers . . . . . . . . . : 10.10.0.10
    DNS Suffix Search List. . . . : corp.redwood
  Wireless LAN adapter Wi-Fi:
    DNS Servers . . . . . . . . . : 8.8.8.8
    DNS Suffix Search List. . . . . : (none)
- nslookup api.internal.redwood 10.10.0.10 -> NXDOMAIN sometimes, other times resolves to 54.23.12.17 (public)
- WireGuard status: interface wg0 up, default route via wg0 present
- Wireshark capture on dock Ethernet: DNS queries are outgoing via Wi‑Fi interface when both NICs present (packets show source MAC = laptop Wi‑Fi adapter).

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Windows DNS resolution uses adapter metric and suffix search list ordering; with both adapters active, queries for single-label or internal hostnames may leave via the Wi‑Fi adapter if suffix ordering/metrics prefer it. Even though WireGuard provides a system-wide default route, DNS queries are performed before the resolver chooses the VPN's DNS or are sent via an adapter with lower metric.
- The Thunderbolt dock sometimes presents itself as a USB Ethernet adapter with a lower interface metric than the Wi‑Fi adapter, which changes behavior after docking/wake. Dock firmware update in Feb may have modified descriptor/driver behavior.
- Split-tunnel policy is set to force all traffic through WireGuard, but the client DNS resolver still sends queries out of the non-VPN adapter when the adapter metric/suffix configuration is inconsistent.
- Some Windows caches (DNS cache, Netsh interface cache) do not refresh until re-dock or adapter disable, causing intermittent persistence of the faulty resolution.

Workarounds found so far:
- Temporary: disabling Wi‑Fi on the laptop forces DNS queries to go over the Ethernet adapter + WireGuard DNS and immediately fixes resolution.
- Alternately, toggling WireGuard off/on or running "ipconfig /flushdns" + "netsh interface ipv4 set dnsservers \"Ethernet\" static 10.10.0.10 primary" (forces DNS on Ethernet) fixes until next sleep/dock event.
- Educated users to avoid leaving Wi‑Fi enabled when docking until a permanent fix is available.

Suggested fix directions / next steps:
1) IT/SRE: Confirm dock driver/firmware interactions — roll back or validate the Feb dock firmware change (Dell WD19TB/WD22).
2) Endpoint team: Evaluate setting DNS registration/order via Intune policy to ensure dock Ethernet has higher DNS priority and correct suffix list when docked (set interface metric and DNS servers via policy).
3) Client-side WireGuard config: ensure DNS settings are pushed to the Windows resolver via the recommended Windows integration (WG tunnel should register DNS to the system resolver and override adapter-level DNS when UP).
4) Add a small startup script in the short term for affected users that runs on connect/dock event: run "netsh interface ipv4 set dnsservers \"Ethernet\" static 10.10.0.10 primary" and "ipconfig /flushdns".
5) Create monitoring/alerting: detect multiple NICs with conflicting DNS servers on corporate devices and open automated tickets.

Action items assigned (triage):
- IT Ops (Evan Kim): Collect 3 reproducible packet captures and ipconfig outputs from affected users by 2026-03-12. (in progress)
- Endpoint (Priya Nair): Draft Intune policy that sets Ethernet DNS priority and deploy to pilot group by 2026-03-19.
- Network (Marco Ruiz): Verify if Dock firmware change was rolled Feb 2026 and coordinate Dell support ticket.

Comments:
- "2026-03-10 09:12 - Evan Kim: Reported by 3 users this morning after docking. Symptoms match DNS going out the wrong interface. Captures attached to ticket."
- "2026-03-10 11:04 - Priya Nair: Can repro on my Dell XPS + WD22. Verified that disabling Wi‑Fi fixes it. I'll attempt an Intune configuration to force DNS servers on Ethernet."
- "2026-03-11 08:22 - Marco Ruiz: Filed case with Dell (case# DELL-882911). They requested PCAPs showing DHCP/descriptor. Firmware diff shows change to USB enumeration order in Feb build."
- "2026-03-12 14:35 - Evan Kim: Pilot Intune profile pushed to 5 users; three reported immediate fix. Expanding pilot to 20 users Friday."

Resolution / status notes:
- Partial workaround validated via Intune policy pilot (forcing Ethernet DNS) that resolves the issue for docked devices when policy applies. Full root cause likely interaction between dock firmware and Windows adapter metric selection; Dell case open.
- Status: In Progress. Tracking rollout and waiting on Dell firmware response.

Follow ups / retrospective items:
- If Dell provides a firmware fix, test with pilot and then schedule staged update for SF office docks.
- Add an automated check in our device onboarding that asserts DNS server alignment when both Wi‑Fi and Ethernet adapters are present.

Attachments: list of PCAP filenames and sanitized ipconfig outputs (stored in support attachments store, links added to ticket).
